title: Geechee Robinson's moon-driven mood changes
summary: Albert describes bandsman Geechee Robinson, who turned Jekyll-and-Hyde and picked arguments at certain times of the month; he later went with Fletcher.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay, and we're at 910 Royal Street, so we're going to just proceed on. One time you mentioned something to me, and I don't want to mention it by the day, but I thought it was a very interesting point, something that the psychologists talk about. That is, how the guys, some people will change, like they're, with the moon, as the moon changes. Right. And they, what about the man in your band that did that?

I don't know, Dick, but I assume that he is. After he left my band, he went a little while with Fletcher when Fletcher was on the road. He was always a fickle fellow, wanting a gold, gold, gold, so I imagine he just kept running. And I never heard from him, he's one of the characters that never did Carl Strawn much.
Yeah. But what did he do when the moon changed? Can you tell me?

Well, we could, that's what we said, the musicians in the band, we'll joke how it would. Well, he's, his attitude would change, well, we said like a Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, he'd get off of the beautiful way he lived, and then he'd just pick arguments with anyone in the band. And that's how we knew that we had to stay clear of him a little, anyhow.
Would that be when the moon was full?
Well, we never paid too much.

Well, you know, that is true. A lot of people do change. Like, some people have moods during the course of the day. Right, right, right. Like, some guys get low every afternoon. Have you noticed that?
Right, right. Well, that's the attitude that this fellow had. Yeah. At a certain time of the month, he would just automatically change.
